title: Accounts Payable Assistant
description:
The Opportunity

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an Accounts Payable Administrator to join a well-established, financially stable and growing family-owned business with a strong reputation for looking after its people.

With a history spanning almost 80 years and continued year-on-year growth, the business offers the stability of an established organisation alongside the opportunity to be part of an evolving finance function. Significant investment is currently being made in systems, technology and process improvement, creating an exciting time to join the team.

You'll play an important role in ensuring the accounts payable function operates accurately, efficiently and to a high standard, while working alongside a supportive and experienced finance team.

What You'll Be Doing
- Processing a high volume of supplier and subcontractor invoices accurately and efficiently.
- Checking invoices, coding and approvals and ensuring appropriate financial controls are followed.
- Reconciling supplier statements and resolving queries and discrepancies.
- Supporting regular supplier payment runs and maintaining strong supplier relationships.
- Assisting with month-end close and related reconciliations.
- Working collaboratively with operational teams, suppliers and the wider finance function.
- Identifying opportunities to improve processes, reduce manual work and increase efficiency.
- Supporting the ongoing implementation of new systems and automation.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone with previous Accounts Payable or Purchase Ledger experience who takes real pride in accuracy and understands the importance of good financial controls.

Why Join?

This is more than simply an invoice-processing role. You'll be joining a business that is growing, investing and actively looking at better ways of working.

The finance function is going through significant systems and process improvements, with automation expected to dramatically reduce manual processing. This creates the opportunity to develop your skills, take on greater responsibility and become involved in more value-added finance activities over time.

Alongside a competitive salary, you'll benefit from a hybrid working arrangement, annual salary reviews, enhanced benefits and genuine long-term progression opportunities.

If you're looking for a role where you can build a career rather than simply process invoices, this is an excellent opportunity to join a successful business at an exciting stage of its growth.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Are you a confident Credit Controller who knows how to navigate the world of council payments and gaining invoice payment from local authorities? If you understand the complexities of the public sector payment process and have the persistence to turn outstanding invoices into cash, this could be the opportunity you've been waiting for!
We're working with a successful and growing business looking for an experienced Credit Controller to take ownership of outstanding debt, build strong relationships with councils and keep cash flowing in the right direction.
What's the role all about?
This isn't just about sending statements and chasing overdue invoices. You'll play a key role in managing the company's debtor ledger, with a particular focus on collecting outstanding payments from councils, local authorities and other public sector organisations.
You'll need to be comfortable navigating complex payment processes, dealing with multiple stakeholders and understanding why public sector invoices can sometimes take longer than expected to settle. More importantly, you'll know when to be diplomatic, when to be persistent and how to get results without damaging valuable customer relationships.
Your responsibilities will include:
Managing and reducing aged debt across a portfolio of customer accounts.
Proactively chasing outstanding invoices with councils and local authorities.
Investigating payment delays, resolving invoice queries and addressing discrepancies.
Building effective working relationships with finance teams and accounts payable departments.
Reconciling customer accounts and allocating payments accurately.
Monitoring credit limits, identifying potential risks and escalating problem accounts.
Producing regular aged debt reports and providing updates on collection performance.
Working closely with internal finance and operational teams to resolve issues quickly.
What are we looking for?
You'll already have experience in a credit control role, ideally with demonstrable success collecting debt from councils, local authorities or wider public sector organisations.
You'll be an excellent communicator, highly organised and resilient enough to keep chasing when payments don't arrive as expected. You'll also have a keen eye for detail, strong reconciliation skills and the confidence to manage difficult conversations professionally.
If you enjoy taking ownership, solving problems and seeing the tangible results of your efforts, this role offers the chance to make a real difference to cash flow and working capital.
If you know your way around public sector debt collection and are ready for your next challenge, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Finance & Payroll Accounts Assistant - TEMP TO PERM
description:
Finance & Payroll Accounts Assistant - TEMP TO PERM

Hours: 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Location: Bourton-on-the-Water
Salary: Up to £35,000
Working pattern: Office-based, with some flexibility around start and finish times

The Role

We are looking for an organised and detail-focused Finance & Payroll Accounts Assistant. The role combines responsibility for accurate weekly payroll preparation with finance, accounts and general administrative support.

The key focus is compiling, checking and validating employee hours before weekly payroll is processed. This is not an end-to-end payroll position; payroll processing, tax and final payroll preparation are handled by an established payroll specialist.

Key Responsibilities
- Compile and validate weekly employee hours, including variable hours, pay rates, sickness, holidays and other payroll adjustments.
- Review time-recording information and compare reports across multiple systems.
- Investigate discrepancies, missing or incorrect information and liaise with managers to resolve issues.
- Ensure payroll data is accurate, complete and correctly allocated ahead of the weekly payroll deadline.
- Support Finance with payroll reporting, reconciliations, financial records and general accounts administration.
- Handle relevant cash, petty cash and payment administration.
- Maintain accurate payroll, financial and employee records, spreadsheets and internal systems.
- Respond to payroll, finance and employee queries professionally, working collaboratively with Finance, HR and management.
- Provide general administrative support to the wider business as required.

What We're Looking For
- Previous payroll experience, with a proven understanding of payroll processes and experience collating and/or checking payroll data.
- Strong Excel skills, including confidence working with formulas, checking formula accuracy and analysing spreadsheets.
- Experience analysing data from multiple systems or reports and confidently interrogating information to identify discrepancies or errors.
- Understanding of hours worked, pay rates, gross pay, deductions, net pay, holiday, sickness and different working arrangements.
- Experience in basic finance and accounts administration, including maintaining financial records, reconciliations and cash-related queries.
- Excellent attention to detail, numerical accuracy and a methodical approach.
- Comfortable working to a weekly payroll cycle and fixed deadlines while maintaining accuracy in a busy environment.
- Strong organisation and prioritisation skills, with the ability to work independently and take ownership of deadlines.
- Good communication skills and confidence liaising with employees and managers.

Working Arrangements

The position is predominantly office-based, Monday to Friday, with some flexibility around start and finish times, provided business requirements and weekly payroll deadlines are met.

The role works across Finance, HR and management, requiring effective communication and collaboration.

Benefits
- Competitive salary up to £35,000.
- 20 days' holiday plus Bank Holidays.
- Pension scheme.
- Lifestyle benefits and retail discounts.
- Employee Assistance Programme.
- Career development opportunities.
- Option to purchase additional annual leave.
- Electric vehicle salary-sacrifice scheme.
- Cycle-to-work scheme.

- How many years' payroll experience you have.
- Your level of Excel experience.
- Your location and how you would travel to Bourton-on-the-Water.
- Your salary expectations.
- Your availability to start.
